To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

new pyrrolocarbazoles in which an imidazole ring is replaced by a five-membered ring bearing a carbonyl group and a six-membered aromatic heterocycle bearing two carbonyl groups have been synthesized and their checkpoint kinase 1 inhibitory properties and antiproliferate activities toward three tumor cells lines have been determined.
the replacement of the imidazole by a five-membered carbonyl ring in granulatimides leads to the formation of potent Chk1 inhibitor compounds.

the replacement of the imidazole ring by a five- and six-membered ring in which the nitrogen is replaced by an oxygen atom and which bears carbonyl functions leads to compounds with higher potency than that of granulatimides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new compounds structurally related to the pyrrolocarbazole derivative granulatimida.
the design, synthesis, and biological activity evaluation of new Chk1 inhibitors structurally similar to the lead compound granulatimides.
the design and synthesis of a new class of Chk1 inhibitors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the replacement of the imidazole with a quinone or hydroquinone moiety in the pyrrolocarbazole ring and the presence of an hydroxyl group on the indolic ring are favorable for the Chk1 inhibitory potency of the compounds, whereas the replacement of the pyrrolyl ring with an oxo- or a methylene group is not favorable for the ChkB inhibitory activity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the quinone and the hydroquinone are more suitable replacements for the imidazole ring than the pyrazine and the piperazine.
